case_number: Civil Appeal Nos. 7812-7814 of 2022 (Arising out of SLP (C) Nos. 31288-31290 of 2011)
summary: The case involved a dispute over whether certain Muslim religious institutions are public trusts under the Bombay Public Trust Act, 1950 or wakfs under the Wakf Act, 1995 and Mohammedan Law. The key issue was the validity of the constitution of the Maharashtra State Board of Wakfs and the transfer of wakfs from the jurisdiction of the Charity Commissioner to the Board. The Charity Commissioner issued a circular in 2003 stating that registered wakfs should not be tried under the Bombay Public Trust Act per Section 43 of the Wakf Act, 1995. Challenges were raised to the Board's formation and the survey process. The High Court stayed the circular and restrained the Board from collecting contributions. A government committee was formed in 2004 to study inter-state models and classify trusts as Shia or Sunni wakfs. The Supreme Court considered the legal validity of the Board and administrative actions taken under the Wakf Act.
final_judgment: The appeals were disposed of by a common judgment, but the final disposition details are not explicitly stated in the provided text.
